You are a coding agent working in a local checkout of b70-inference-server, an LLM inference engine for the Intel Arc Pro B70 written in C++ with Level Zero kernels, plus Python and shell tooling. The repository is at /work.

You help the user with software engineering tasks: finding code, explaining it, editing it and running builds and tests. Use the tools you are given to inspect the repository; never guess the contents of a file you have not read. Prefer grep and glob to locate code, read to look at it, edit to change it (the oldString must match the file exactly, including indentation) and bash to run commands.

Guidelines:
- Be concise. Do not explain what you are about to do at length; act.
- Make one tool call at a time and wait for its result.
- Keep edits minimal and in the style of the surrounding code.
- Paths passed to tools are absolute and start with /work.
- The C++ tree builds with CMake into /work/build; tests are ctest targets named after their source file (for example tests/prefill/dequant_test.cc is dequant_test). The Python tools run with python3 and their tests with python3 -m pytest.
- Do not commit, push or change git state unless the user asks.
Rename `info` to `info_val` in /work/src/loader/loader.cc, only the one defined on line 142.

00125| // Small tensors: the model description's table is walked, never second-guessed.

00131| size_t bake_elem_bytes(model::SmallBake b) {

00140| const uint8_t* small_src(NameView& v, const SafetensorsSet& set, const std::string& full,

00155| // The bakes themselves (docs/13-loader.md "What the loader bakes in").
00156| void bake_small(const model::SmallTensor& t, const uint8_t* src, uint8_t* dst, Widen& widen) {
00157|   const size_t n = t.elems;
00158|   const uint16_t* w = reinterpret_cast<const uint16_t*>(src);
00159|   std::vector<float> f;
00160|   switch (t.bake) {
00161|     case model::SmallBake::PlainBf16:
00162|       // RMSNormGated: plain w, and bf16 - the reference's own parameter dtype
00163|       // is bf16 and it multiplies in the bf16 domain, so widening would move
00164|       // away from the oracle rather than towards it.
00165|       std::memcpy(dst, src, n * 2);
00166|       return;
00167|     case model::SmallBake::OnePlusWFp32:
00168|       // Gemma-style RMSNorm: x*rsqrt(mean(x^2)+eps)*(1 + w). The reference does
00169|       // the whole product in fp32, so the `+1` is added in fp32 and STORED
00170|       // fp32 - no cast back to bf16, which removes a rounding the oracle never
00171|       // had (up to 0.39% on a multiplier near 1). Ruling 2026-08-25.
00172|       f.resize(n);
00173|       for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) f[i] = 1.0f + common::bf16_to_f32(w[i]);
00174|       widen.norm += n * 2;
00175|       break;
00176|     case model::SmallBake::NegExpFp32:
00177|       // The GDN decay is only ever used as exp(g) with
00178|       // g = -exp(A_log) * softplus(a + dt_bias): the exp is a per-head
00179|       // constant, hoisted out of 48 layers x every token.
00180|       f.resize(n);
00181|       for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) f[i] = -std::exp(common::bf16_to_f32(w[i]));
00182|       widen.gdn += n * 2;
00183|       break;
00184|     case model::SmallBake::RawFp32Widen:
00185|       // The recurrence and the 4-tap depthwise conv accumulate in fp32:
00186|       // widening once at load saves a convert per tap per token.
00187|       f.resize(n);
00188|       for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) f[i] = common::bf16_to_f32(w[i]);
00189|       widen.gdn += n * 2;
00190|       break;
00191|     case model::SmallBake::RawFp32:
00192|       std::memcpy(dst, src, n * 4);   // already fp32 in the checkpoint
00193|       return;
00194|   }
00195|   std::memcpy(dst, f.data(), n * 4);
00196| }
